July I2, I96I
Mr. Herold M. Bixby
Bolton Landing, New York
Dear Mr. Bixby:
Mr. Willis Combs of Sanibel, Florida has written of your
interest of a piece of land on Sanibel (234
acres) that is surrounded by
State and Federal land and would be a desirable addition to the wildlife
As you may know there have been two very favorable developments
in the land preservation picture in Plorida in recent months.
A committee
composed of the heads of several of the State's
resource management agencies,-
Board of Parks, Game and Fish Commission, Conservation Dept. 80. is working on
a land classification program with the object of classifying the remaining
undeveloped land according to its best potential uses, with land for wildlife and
the important objectives.
As urance has been given that no
that might be of value for these purposes will be sold until
classification has been agreed on, and that efforts will also ibe made to preserve
privately owned land that has special value.
In May a law was passed which would enable the U.S. Fish & Wildlife
Service to purchase land for use as wildlife refuges in Floride.
This has been
prevented by Florida law for several years. There is money available for such
purchases now, and the Fish and Wildlife Service has under consideration some
areas which it has been studying. I know that both the State authorities and
Mr. Walter Gresh, head of the U.S.F..W.L. ofride in Atlanta are interested in
strengthening and developing the refuge area on Sanibel.
I am sure that any
local interest or help that might be shown toward that end would be very helpful.
I know that the State program which which was to be started on a trial basis
in a few loaalities this past pring was planned to depend heavily on local
help, since goverrment purchases of all the needed land would be impossible.
I understand that there might be an active interest on Sanibel and
Captiva for a project of this kind. Mr. William Kida,administrative assistant
in the Governor's
office in Tallahassee, is in charge of this program for the
Governor, and Mr. Walter A. Gresh, regional head of the U.S.F.EW.L. Service ,
Peachtree-seventh Bldg. Atlanta,Go. has charge of the Federal progrem. I believe
you would find them both interested and cooperative.
MIss MA SO VON BOROWSKY
JOHNN STORER
